newsitem.title: USA: Study says mental stress worsens heart problems.
newsitem.headline: Study says mental stress worsens heart problems.

text.p: The mental stresses felt in everyday life can worsen heart problems for heart patients who must already watch how they exercise, a study said Tuesday.

In the Duke University study of 132 heart patients, negative feelings such as tension, frustration and sadness more than doubled their risk during the subsequent hour of suffering an episode of myocardial ishcemia, or insufficient blood flow to the heart.

Heavy exercise was also found to be a powerful trigger of myocardial ischemia, which can lead to more dire heart problems, wrote researcher Elizabeth Gullette in the Journal of the American Medical Association.
Conversely, positive emotions such as feelings of happiness reduced the risk of ischemia only slightly, she wrote.

In an accompanying editorial, Murray Mittleman and Malcolm Maclure of Harvard University said the danger to heart patients from extreme stress created by cataclysmic events, such as earthquakes and wars, "presented only the tip of the iceberg."

"Whether these low levels of stress are capable of triggering the more dire consequences of (coronary artery disease), such as myocardial infarction (heart attack) or sudden cardiac death, requires further study," they wrote.
In the latest study, researchers followed the patients in ordinary, out-of-hospital settings, and produced similar results to previous research in laboratory settings.
Gullette wrote that her results suggested that heart patients should receive training in how to manage stress as well as learning proper exercise regimes, and not merely undergo drug therapy.
